name: Bánh căn
summary: Small rice cakes grilled over charcoal in Da Lat, topped with an egg, eaten in the morning or as a snack.
origin: A Da Lat cake Vietnam Tourism traces to Hue bánh bèo. The Da Lat version is grilled over a charcoal brazier.
texture: Vietnam Tourism calls the cakes bite-size. Bánh Căn Lệ’s listing says the shell is crisp.
howToEat: Vietnam Tourism says eat it early, as breakfast or a light snack, with a quail egg or a duck egg on the cake. One article says the dip is an onion sauce.

Visit Lâm Đồng listings add other fillings and dips, and they do not agree with each other. Cây Bơ names quail egg, chicken egg, meat, shrimp, and a soft-yolk egg, with mắm nêm or xíu mại sauce. Lệ names minced beef, quail egg, chicken egg, and seafood, with fish sauce or mắm nêm. The door called Bánh căn Đà Lạt names quail egg, minced beef, and chicken egg, with xíu mại sauce and fish sauce. A Cát names chicken egg, chicken with beef, quail egg, quail egg with beef, seafood, chicken with squid, and quail egg with oyster, plus xíu mại and pickled vegetables.
where: Vietnam Tourism puts the cakes in the centre, especially around Hoa Binh.

Visit Lâm Đồng prints 56 Tăng Bạt Hổ, open 06:00–11:30; 7 Tăng Bạt Hổ, open 16:00–23:00; and 27/44 Yersin, open 06:00–19:00. A Cát is at H55 KQH Nguyễn Thị Nghĩa, also written H54-55. That listing prints 08:00–23:59 in the header and 07:00–21:30 in the text.
priceBand: Visit Lâm Đồng prints 15,000–30,000 VND at Cây Bơ and at Lệ, 20,000–50,000 VND at 7 Tăng Bạt Hổ, and “Đang cập nhật” at A Cát. Cây Bơ also prints 30,000 VND for five pairs, and Lệ’s text says 25,000 VND. Vietnam Tourism prints no price. A single city price is Check on arrival.
